from.description: Source URL returned by the list redirects endpoint.

actions.name: hosting_install_ssl
actions.description:
Install SSL. Requests a lifetime SSL certificate for the website. The installation runs in the background;
`Get SSL status` reports `active` or `failed` when it ends. An `active` lifetime certificate
does not block the request: a new installation is requested, which is how a certificate is
reinstalled.

Returns 422 for free subdomains (their certificate is managed by the platform), while an
installation is `installing` or `waiting_for_retry`, when the website's certificate was
revoked (it cannot be reissued), and when an uploaded custom certificate is installed; that
one has to be uninstalled first.

actions.name: hosting_get_ssl_status
actions.description:
Get SSL status. Returns the SSL state of the website: the certificate `status` and `provider`, whether the
certificate is a lifetime one managed by the platform, whether HTTP requests are redirected to
HTTPS, when the certificate stops being valid and the last installation error.

`installing` and `waiting_for_retry` mean an installation is in progress. `failed` means the
last installation gave up, or the website was not updated for 60 minutes while `installing`;
`last_error` holds the reason when it is a known message, otherwise it is null. `expired`
means the assigned certificate's validity has ended. `not_installed` means no certificate is
assigned. Free subdomains use a platform-manag...

actions.name: hosting_toggle_https_redirect
actions.description:
Toggle HTTPS redirect. Turns the HTTP to HTTPS redirect of the website on or off, based on `is_enabled`. Does
nothing when the redirect is already in the requested state. Turning it on requires an
installed certificate (`status` `active` or `expired` on `Get SSL status`) and returns 422
when there is none; turning it off is always accepted.

is_enabled.description: Turn the HTTP to HTTPS redirect on (true) or off (false) for the website.

actions.name: hosting_uninstall_ssl
actions.description:
Uninstall SSL. Removes the SSL certificate assigned to the website, turns the HTTPS redirect off and cancels
a pending installation retry. The website serves plain HTTP until a new installation
completes. `Get SSL status` reports `not_installed` as soon as the call returns; the call also
succeeds when no certificate is assigned, so repeating it is safe.

Returns 422 for free subdomains (their certificate is managed by the platform) and while an
installation is `installing`.

actions.name: hosting_list_websites
actions.description:
List websites. Retrieve a paginated list of websites (CloudLinux, Builder, and Horizons) accessible to the
authenticated client.

This endpoint returns websites from your hosting accounts as well as
websites from other client hosting accounts that have shared access
with you.

Each website includes a `website_type` field describing the type of
website detected on the underlying platform (`wordpress`, `builder`,
`horizons`, `nodejs`, or `other`). Some fields, such as
`vhost_type`, `username`, and `root_directory`, only apply to
CloudLinux websites and are null for other platforms.

Use `website_types` to list only websites of a given detected type, e.g. only
WordPress websites (`website_ty...

domain.description: Filter by domain name (case-insensitive substring match)

website_types.description: Filter by detected website type, e.g. wordpress,nodejs. Accepts a comma-separated list.

actions.name: hosting_deploy_static_site_archive
actions.description:
Deploy static site archive. Deploy a static application from an archive file.

WARNING: this overwrites the website's existing contents and cannot be undone —
verify this is intended before calling this endpoint.

This endpoint allows you to deploy a static application from an archive
file that has been uploaded to the website's directory.

This only works for static sites (pre-built HTML/CSS/JS with no build step). For
Node.js applications, use `Create NodeJS build from archive` instead, or
`Start Node.js build` if the archive is already uploaded. For WordPress sites,
use `Import WordPress website`.

archive_path.description: Relative path to the archive file from website root directory

actions.name: hosting_delete_website
actions.description:
Delete website. This endpoint permanently removes a website and all of its data. This action
cannot be undone. Before calling it, make sure the user understands the
consequences and explicitly confirms that they want to proceed.

All website files, databases and related configuration will be removed.
The hosting plan itself is kept, so a new website can be created on it afterwards.

Supported websites: main and addon domain websites on web hosting plans, and
Website Builder websites. Parked domains and subdomains cannot be deleted with
this endpoint. The domain must be the exact website domain, not a preview
domain or an alias.

Returns 404 when the domain does not exist or does not belon...

actions.name: mail_create_alias
actions.description:
Create alias. Create an alias for the given mailbox. The alias address is formed
from the given local part and the domain of the mailbox. Messages
sent to the alias are delivered to the mailbox.

local_part.description: Local part of the alias address (the part before the @). The domain is taken from the mailbox. Case-insensitive and stored lowercase; must start and end with a letter or digit; single dots, underscores and hyphens are allowed in between.

actions.name: mail_delete_alias
actions.description:
Delete alias. Delete an alias. Messages sent to the alias address are no longer
delivered to the mailbox.

actions.name: mail_list_aliases
actions.description:
List aliases. Retrieve a paginated list of aliases across all mailboxes of a mail
order.

actions.name: mail_create_api_token
actions.description:
Create API token. Create an API token for the given mail order. The token grants access
to the [Hostinger Email API](https://api.mail.hostinger.com/), where
you can provision and manage the mailboxes it is scoped to.

The plaintext token is returned only in this response, never again.
A maximum of 10 tokens can exist per order. Use
`scope.has_all_mailboxes` to cover all current and future mailboxes,
or list specific mailboxes in `scope.mailbox_ids`.

name.description: Human-readable label for this token

scope.description: Mailbox scope this token can access

has_all_mailboxes.description: Grant access to all current and future mailboxes of the order

mailbox_ids.description: Required when `has_all_mailboxes` is false. Mailbox resource IDs of this order.

actions.name: mail_revoke_api_token
actions.description:
Revoke API token. Revoke an API token. The token immediately loses access to the
[Hostinger Email API](https://api.mail.hostinger.com/). This action
cannot be undone.

tokenId.description: API token ID (returned when the token was created)

actions.name: mail_list_api_tokens
actions.description:
List API tokens. Retrieve a paginated list of
[Hostinger Email API](https://api.mail.hostinger.com/) tokens across
all your mail orders, optionally filtered by order. Plaintext tokens
are never included; they are returned only when a token is created.

order_id.description: Filter tokens by order resource ID. Single value or comma-separated list.

actions.name: mail_create_autoreply
actions.description:
Create autoreply. Create an automatic reply for the given mailbox. A mailbox can have
only one autoreply. Omit `starts_at` to activate the autoreply
immediately and omit `ends_at` to keep it active indefinitely.

display_name.description: Sender display name used for the reply

starts_at.description: When the autoreply becomes active. Defaults to now.

ends_at.description: When the autoreply stops. Omit for an indefinite autoreply.

actions.name: mail_update_autoreply
actions.description:
Update autoreply. Replace the autoreply with the given content and schedule. Omitted
optional fields are cleared: omit `starts_at` to activate the
autoreply immediately and omit `ends_at` to keep it active
indefinitely.

display_name.description: Sender display name used for the reply

starts_at.description: When the autoreply becomes active. Defaults to now.

ends_at.description: When the autoreply stops. Omit for an indefinite autoreply.

actions.name: mail_delete_autoreply
actions.description:
Delete autoreply. Delete the autoreply of a mailbox. The mailbox stops sending
automatic replies immediately.

actions.name: mail_list_autoreplies
actions.description:
List autoreplies. Retrieve a paginated list of autoreplies across all mailboxes of a
mail order.

actions.name: mail_create_catch_all
actions.description:
Create catch-all. Create a catch-all that routes all messages sent to unknown addresses
of the domain to the given mailbox. The mailbox address receives a
confirmation email and the catch-all becomes active only after it is
confirmed. A domain can have only one catch-all.

actions.name: mail_delete_catch_all
actions.description:
Delete catch-all. Delete a catch-all. Messages sent to unknown addresses of the domain
are no longer routed to the mailbox.

actions.name: mail_list_catch_alls
actions.description:
List catch-alls. Retrieve a paginated list of catch-alls across all mailboxes of a
mail order.

actions.name: mail_resend_catch_all_confirmation
actions.description:
Resend catch-all confirmation. Resend the confirmation email to the mailbox address of an
unconfirmed catch-all.

actions.name: mail_create_forwarder
actions.description:
Create forwarder. Create a forwarder from the given mailbox to the destination address.
The destination receives a confirmation email and forwarding becomes
active only after it is confirmed.

destination.description: Email address the messages will be forwarded to

is_keep_copy_enabled.description: Whether to keep a copy of forwarded messages in the mailbox. Defaults to false.

actions.name: mail_delete_forwarder
actions.description:
Delete forwarder. Delete a forwarder. The mailbox stops forwarding messages to the
destination address immediately.

actions.name: mail_list_forwarders
actions.description:
List forwarders. Retrieve a paginated list of forwarders across all mailboxes of a
mail order.

actions.name: mail_resend_forwarder_confirmation
actions.description:
Resend forwarder confirmation. Resend the confirmation email to the destination address of an
unconfirmed forwarder.

actions.name: mail_update_forwarder_keep_copy_setting
actions.description:
Update forwarder keep-copy setting. Enable or disable keeping a copy of forwarded messages in the
mailbox.

is_keep_copy_enabled.description: Whether to keep a copy of forwarded messages in the mailbox

actions.name: mail_list_access_logs
actions.description:
List access logs. Retrieve paginated access logs for the domain attached to the given
mail order. Supports filtering by account, date range, protocol,
status, and deletion flag. Results are sorted by timestamp descending.

account.description: Filter log entries by a specific email account

date.description: Exact date filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Takes precedence over `from_date`/`to_date` when both are given.

protocol.description: Filter access log entries by protocol

has_deletions.description: Filter access log entries by whether the session had deletions

actions.name: mail_list_action_logs
actions.description:
List action logs. Retrieve paginated account action logs (administrative and user
actions) for the given mail order. Supports filtering by account,
date range, and status. Results are sorted by timestamp descending.

account.description: Filter log entries by a specific email account

date.description: Exact date filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Takes precedence over `from_date`/`to_date` when both are given.

actions.name: mail_list_inbound_logs
actions.description:
List inbound logs. Retrieve paginated inbound (received mail) delivery logs for the
domain attached to the given mail order. Supports filtering by
account, date range, status, sender, and recipient. Results are
sorted by timestamp descending.

account.description: Filter log entries by a specific email account

date.description: Exact date filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Takes precedence over `from_date`/`to_date` when both are given.

sender.description: Filter log entries by sender. Accepts a full email address or a domain.

recipient.description: Filter log entries by recipient. Accepts a full email address or a domain.

actions.name: mail_list_mailbox_action_logs
actions.description:
List mailbox action logs. Retrieve paginated mailbox action logs (message and mailbox events)
for a mailbox in the given mail order. The mailbox email must belong
to the order's domain. Supports date range and event type filters.
Results are sorted by timestamp descending.

email.description: Mailbox email address. Must belong to the order's domain.

date.description: Exact date filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Takes precedence over `from_date`/`to_date` when both are given.

event.description: Filter mailbox action log entries by event type

actions.name: mail_list_outbound_logs
actions.description:
List outbound logs. Retrieve paginated outbound (sent mail) delivery logs for the domain
attached to the given mail order. Supports filtering by account, date
range, status, sender, and recipient. Results are sorted by timestamp
descending.

account.description: Filter log entries by a specific email account

date.description: Exact date filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Takes precedence over `from_date`/`to_date` when both are given.

sender.description: Filter log entries by sender. Accepts a full email address or a domain.

recipient.description: Filter log entries by recipient. Accepts a full email address or a domain.

actions.name: mail_list_mailboxes
actions.description:
List mailboxes. Retrieve a paginated list of mailboxes belonging to a mail order.

Use this endpoint to monitor mailboxes of your mail service, including
their status, enabled protocols, attached resource counts, and
periodically synced usage numbers (usage may lag behind live values).

search.description: Filter mailboxes whose email address contains the given string

sort.description: Sort mailboxes by field. Prefix with `-` for descending order.

actions.name: mail_create_mailbox
actions.description:
Create mailbox. Create a mailbox under the given mail order. The full email address is
composed from the given local part and the domain of the order.

local_part.description: Local part of the mailbox address (the part before the @). The domain is taken from the order. Must start and end with a letter or digit; single dots, underscores and hyphens are allowed in between.

password.description: Mailbox password. Minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number and special character.

actions.name: mail_delete_mailbox
actions.description:
Delete mailbox. Delete a mailbox. The mailbox is soft-deleted and stays restorable
for a limited period before it is permanently removed.

actions.name: mail_change_mailbox_password
actions.description: Change mailbox password. Change the password of a mailbox.

password.description: New mailbox password. Minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number and special character; must not be a commonly used password.

actions.name: mail_list_orders
actions.description:
List orders. Retrieve a paginated list of mail orders associated with your account.

Use this endpoint to monitor your mail services, including their status,
plan, attached domain, and expiration details.

domain.description: Filter orders by domain name (exact match)

sort.description: Sort orders by field. Prefix with `-` for descending order.

actions.name: mail_get_order_plan
actions.description:
Get order plan. Retrieve the plan the given mail order was purchased with, including
domain-level and mailbox-level quotas, limits, and protocol
availability.

actions.name: mail_create_webhook
actions.description:
Create webhook. Create a webhook for the given mailbox. The generated secret is
returned only in this response and is sent as a bearer token with
every delivery.

name.description: Human-readable name for this webhook

description.description: Optional description of the webhook's purpose

url.description: Publicly reachable URL that receives the webhook POST requests

actions.name: mail_list_webhook_delivery_logs
actions.description:
List webhook delivery logs. Retrieve a paginated list of webhook delivery logs for the given mail
order, including delivery outcome, duration, and retry counts.
Supports filtering by mailbox.

mailbox_id.description: Filter by the mailbox resource ID the webhooks are attached to

actions.name: mail_get_webhook
actions.description:
Get webhook. Retrieve the details of a single webhook. The webhook secret is never
included; it is returned only when a webhook is created or its secret
is regenerated.

webhookId.description: Webhook ID (returned when the webhook was created)

actions.name: mail_delete_webhook
actions.description:
Delete webhook. Permanently delete a webhook. This action cannot be undone. After
deletion the URL no longer receives event notifications.

webhookId.description: Webhook ID (returned when the webhook was created)

actions.name: mail_update_webhook
actions.description:
Update webhook. Partially update a webhook. Only the fields included in the request
body are changed; omitted fields retain their current values. Pass
`"description": null` to clear the description.

webhookId.description: Webhook ID (returned when the webhook was created)

name.description: New human-readable name for the webhook

description.description: New description, or null to clear it

events.description: Replaces the full list of subscribed events

url.description: New URL to deliver events to

actions.name: mail_list_webhooks
actions.description:
List webhooks. Retrieve a paginated list of webhooks belonging to the given mail
order. Supports filtering by mailbox and status. The webhook secret
is never included; it is returned only when a webhook is created or
its secret is regenerated.

mailbox_id.description: Filter by the mailbox resource ID the webhooks are attached to

actions.name: mail_regenerate_webhook_secret
actions.description:
Regenerate webhook secret. Regenerate the secret of a webhook. The previous secret is
immediately invalidated. The new secret is returned only in this
response and is sent as a bearer token with every delivery.

webhookId.description: Webhook ID (returned when the webhook was created)

actions.name: mail_test_webhook
actions.description:
Test webhook. Send a test delivery to the webhook URL and return the result. Test
requests are rate limited upstream.

webhookId.description: Webhook ID (returned when the webhook was created)

actions.name: reach_get_automation_details
actions.description:
Get automation details. Get a single automation with the counts of contacts that entered it, are moving through it,
finished it or failed on the way.

This describes the automation itself. To see the workflow it runs, use the steps endpoint.

actions.name: reach_list_automations
actions.description:
List automations. Get a paginated list of the automations in a profile.

Every automation comes with the counts of contacts that entered it, are moving through it,
finished it or failed on the way. Those counts describe the contact journey and are not
email engagement metrics - for opens, clicks and unsubscribes use the campaign statistics
endpoint instead.

status.description:
Filter automations by status.

There is no `completed` status. An automation that has finished for every contact still
reports `active`.

sort_direction.description: Order automations by creation date. Newest first unless set to `asc`.

actions.name: reach_list_automation_steps
actions.description:
List automation steps. Get the workflow of an automation as a flat list of steps.

The steps form a tree rather than a straight line: follow `parent_uuid` to reconstruct the
branches, and use `step_order` to order the steps that share a parent. An automation with no
steps yet returns an empty list.

actions.name: reach_get_campaign_details
actions.description:
Get campaign details. Get a single campaign with its sender, subject, template reference, targeting and delivery
progress.

This describes how the campaign was set up and how far it has got. For opens, clicks and
unsubscribes use the campaign statistics endpoint.

actions.name: reach_list_campaigns
actions.description:
List campaigns. Get a paginated list of the campaigns in a profile.

Each campaign carries its headline engagement rates. Filter by status to find drafts,
scheduled, sending or sent campaigns, keeping in mind that a fully sent campaign has the
status `publish`. By default only regular campaigns are returned - pass `type` to get the
emails sent by automations or the double opt-in confirmations instead.

status.description:
Filter campaigns by status.

A fully sent campaign has the status `publish`. There is no `sent` status, and campaigns can
be neither paused nor archived.

type.description:
Filter campaigns by type.

Defaults to `campaign`, which leaves out the emails sent by automations and the double
opt-in confirmations.

sort_direction.description: Order campaigns by creation date. Newest first unless set to `asc`.

actions.name: reach_create_draft_campaign
actions.description:
Create a draft campaign. Create a campaign in a profile.

The campaign is created as a draft, so nothing is sent and no contact is touched. It has no
audience yet either - targeting and scheduling are not part of this request, the draft is
finished and sent from the Reach interface.

sender_name.description: From name shown to the recipients.

sender_email.description:
From address of the campaign. Its domain has to be verified on the profile before
the campaign can be sent.

title.description: Name the campaign is listed under. Not shown to the recipients.

template_uuid.description:
Template to send, as returned by the template endpoints. Can be left out and
attached later, but the campaign cannot be sent without one.

metadata.description: Extra campaign fields. Any key outside the listed ones is rejected.

preheader.description: Preview text shown after the subject line in the inbox.

source.description: Where the campaign was created from.

actions.name: reach_get_campaign_performance
actions.description:
Get campaign performance. Get the performance of a campaign: delivery, opens, clicks and unsubscribes, with the
matching rates.

Every count is unique contacts rather than raw events, so a contact who opens the same email
five times is counted once.

actions.name: reach_delete_contact_field
actions.description:
Delete a contact field. Delete a custom contact field.

Every value contacts hold for the field is deleted with it, and for the choice types so
are its options. The contacts themselves are not affected.

actions.name: reach_update_contact_field
actions.description:
Update a contact field. Rename a custom contact field and, for the choice types, replace its option set.

Options carrying a uuid are kept and relabelled, options without one are created, and any
existing option left out of the list is deleted along with the values contacts hold for
it. The field type and slug cannot be changed.

options.description: Replaces the option set when provided. Entries carrying a uuid are kept and relabelled, entries without one are created, and any existing option missing from the list is deleted along with the values contacts hold for it.

actions.name: reach_list_contact_fields
actions.description:
List contact fields. Get the custom contact fields defined in a profile.

Custom fields let you store your own attributes on contacts. The returned uuids are what
you pass to the contact update endpoint to set values, and choice fields also list the
options available to pick from.

actions.name: reach_create_contact_field
actions.description:
Create a contact field. Define a new custom contact field in a profile.

The `slug` is derived from the label and, like the field type, cannot be changed later.
Use the returned uuid to set values on contacts.

options.description: Required for single_choice and multi_choice, ignored for the scalar types. Labels must be unique regardless of casing.

actions.name: reach_get_contact_details
actions.description:
Get contact details. Get the full details of a single contact.

Alongside the contact's own attributes this returns the tags assigned to it and the
values it holds for the profile's custom contact fields.

actions.name: reach_delete_profile_contact
actions.description:
Delete a profile contact. Permanently delete a contact from a profile.

The contact is removed together with its custom field values and tag assignments.

actions.name: reach_update_contact
actions.description:
Update a contact's attributes and custom field values.

Only the properties present in the request body are changed, so a partial body is enough
to change a single attribute. Sending a property as `null` clears it.

The response carries the contact's core attributes. Read back its tags, custom field
values, source and note with `GET /api/reach/v1/profiles/{profileUuid}/contacts/{contactUuid}`.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164 format (leading "+" then 7-15 digits)

fields.description: Set custom field values. Omit to leave untouched, send an empty array to clear them all.

actions.name: reach_create_contacts_in_bulk
actions.description:
Create contacts in bulk. Create many contacts in a profile in a single call.

The contacts are imported in the background, so a success response means the import was
accepted rather than finished. Contacts whose email already exists in the profile keep
their current values; only the ones that are still empty, custom fields included, are
filled in. If double opt-in is enabled, new contacts start off pending and are sent a
confirmation email.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164 format (leading "+" then 7-15 digits)

fields.description:
Custom field values to set on the contact. For a contact whose email already
exists, only fields that have no value yet are filled. Unknown field UUIDs and
values that do not match the field type are skipped.

tag_uuids.description: Existing tags to attach to every created contact

note.description: Note applied to every created contact

actions.name: reach_list_profile_contacts
actions.description:
List profile contacts. Get a paginated list of contacts belonging to a profile.

Contacts can be filtered by subscription status, by tag, and by an email search term.
The `meta.total` field of the response is the number of contacts matching the filters,
so calling this endpoint without filters gives the profile's total contact count.

actions.name: reach_create_new_contacts
actions.description:
Create new contacts. Create a new contact in the email marketing system.

This endpoint allows you to create a new contact with basic information like name, email, and surname.

If double opt-in is enabled, the contact will be created with a pending status
and a confirmation email will be sent.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164 format (leading "+" then 7-15 digits)

tag_uuids.description: Existing tags to attach to the created contact

fields.description:
Custom field values to set on the contact. When a contact with this email already exists,
only fields that have no value yet are filled. Unknown field UUIDs and values that do not
match the field type are skipped.

actions.name: reach_count_profile_segment_contacts
actions.description:
Count profile segment contacts. Count the contacts currently matching a segment without listing them.

Cheaper than paging through the segment contacts endpoint when only the size is needed.

actions.name: reach_list_profile_segment_contacts
actions.description:
List profile segment contacts. Retrieve contacts associated with a specific segment for a given profile.

This endpoint allows you to fetch and filter contacts that belong to a particular segment,
identified by its UUID, scoped to a specific profile.

actions.name: reach_get_profile_segment_details
actions.description:
Get profile segment details. Get a single segment of a profile, including the conditions that define it.

To retrieve the contacts currently matching those conditions, use the segment contacts
endpoint instead.

actions.name: reach_update_profile_segment
actions.description:
Update a profile segment. Rename a segment and/or replace the conditions that define it.

`name` is always required. Omit `conditions` to rename without touching the conditions;
supply them and they replace the existing set entirely rather than being merged into it.
Contacts are never modified, but which of them match the segment can change immediately.

conditions.description: Replaces the existing conditions entirely. Omit to keep the current ones.

attribute.description:
A built-in contact attribute, or `cf:{fieldUuid}` to target a custom
contact field. Custom fields are addressed by field UUID; their slug
is not accepted.

Built-in attributes: `email`, `note`, `domain`, `source`,
`opt_in_method`, `subscription_status`, `subscribed_at`,
`unsubscribed_at`, `created_at`, `tag`, `campaigns`, `processed`,
`opened`, `clicked`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `soft_bounced`,
`dropped`.

Which operators are accepted depends on the attribute.

value.description: Always a string, including for numeric and date comparisons

logic.description: How to combine multiple conditions. Required when conditions are given.

actions.name: reach_delete_profile_segment
actions.description:
Delete a profile segment. Delete a segment.

Only the segment definition is removed. The contacts that matched it are left untouched.

actions.name: reach_list_segment_filter_attributes
actions.description:
List segment filter attributes. List every attribute a segment condition can filter on, with the operators each attribute
accepts, the value format they expect and, where the value is constrained, the allowed
values.

The list is profile specific: it includes the profile's custom contact fields, its tags and
its 20 most recently published campaigns, so the valid attributes cannot be hardcoded. Read
it before creating or updating a segment to discover the valid `attribute`, `operator` and
`value` combinations.

actions.name: reach_preview_contacts_matching_conditions
actions.description:
Preview contacts matching conditions. Preview the contacts matching a set of conditions without saving a segment.

The body is the same set of conditions accepted when creating or updating a segment, so this
is how to check who a filter reaches, and how many, before persisting it. Nothing is stored
and no contact is modified.

Call the segment filter attributes endpoint first to discover the valid `attribute`,
`operator` and `value` combinations.

conditions.description: Conditions a contact must satisfy to appear in the preview

attribute.description:
A built-in contact attribute, or `cf:{fieldUuid}` to target a custom
contact field. Which operators are accepted depends on the attribute,
so read the segment filter attributes endpoint for the authoritative
list.

value.description: Always a string, including for numeric and date comparisons

search.description: Narrow the preview to contacts whose email matches

actions.name: reach_list_profile_segments
actions.description:
List profile segments. Get a paginated list of the segments defined in a profile.

Each entry carries the number of contacts currently matching it, which is recalculated on
read rather than stored. Use `count_type` to count either every matching contact or only
the subscribed ones.

count_type.description: Which matching contacts to count for each segment

actions.name: reach_create_profile_segment
actions.description:
Create a profile segment. Create a segment in a profile.

A segment is a saved set of conditions rather than a fixed list, so its membership changes
as contacts change. Creating one does not modify any contact.

conditions.description: Conditions a contact must satisfy to fall into the segment

attribute.description:
A built-in contact attribute, or `cf:{fieldUuid}` to target a custom
contact field. Custom fields are addressed by field UUID; their slug
is not accepted.

Built-in attributes: `email`, `note`, `domain`, `source`,
`opt_in_method`, `subscription_status`, `subscribed_at`,
`unsubscribed_at`, `created_at`, `tag`, `campaigns`, `processed`,
`opened`, `clicked`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `soft_bounced`,
`dropped`.

Which operators are accepted depends on the attribute.

value.description: Always a string, including for numeric and date comparisons

actions.name: reach_assign_contact_to_tag
actions.description:
Assign a contact to a tag. Assign a tag to a single contact.

Unlike the bulk endpoint this is applied immediately rather than queued. Assigning a tag
the contact already carries succeeds without duplicating it.

actions.name: reach_remove_contact_from_tag
actions.description:
Remove a contact from a tag. Remove a tag from a single contact.

Unlike the bulk endpoint this is applied immediately rather than queued. Neither the tag
nor the contact is deleted.

actions.name: reach_assign_contacts_to_tag
actions.description:
Assign contacts to a tag. Assign a tag to many contacts at once.

Pass `contact_uuids` to target specific contacts, or `all_contacts` to target every contact
in the profile. The work is queued, so a success response means it was accepted rather than
finished. Contacts that already carry the tag are left alone.

contact_uuids.description: Contacts to apply the change to. Required unless all_contacts is true.

all_contacts.description: Apply to every contact in the profile

actions.name: reach_remove_contacts_from_tag
actions.description:
Remove contacts from a tag. Remove a tag from many contacts at once.

Pass `contact_uuids` to target specific contacts, or `all_contacts` to target every contact
in the profile. The work is queued, so a success response means it was accepted rather than
finished. The tag itself and the contacts are not deleted.

contact_uuids.description: Contacts to apply the change to. Required unless all_contacts is true.

all_contacts.description: Apply to every contact in the profile

actions.name: reach_delete_tag
actions.description:
Delete a tag and remove it from every contact carrying it.

The contacts themselves are not deleted. This is idempotent: deleting a tag that does not
exist in the profile still succeeds.

actions.name: reach_rename_tag
actions.description:
Rename a tag.

The contacts assigned to the tag are unaffected. Names are unique within a profile, so
renaming a tag to a name that is already taken is rejected.

actions.name: reach_list_profile_tags
actions.description:
List profile tags. Get all tags defined in a profile.

Tags are the way contacts are grouped in Reach, and can be used to filter the contact
list or to build segments.

actions.name: reach_create_or_find_tags
actions.description:
Create or find tags. Create tags in a profile.

Names that already exist in the profile are not duplicated: the existing tag is returned
instead, so the call is safe to repeat. Every tag in the request is returned, whether it
was created now or already existed.

actions.name: reach_get_form_details
actions.description:
Get form details. Get a single form with the URL of its hosted template and the tags it applies to the contacts
it captures.

There is no ready-made embed snippet in the response - either serve the template HTML yourself
or build your own embed around the form uuid.

actions.name: reach_delete_form
actions.description:
Delete form. Permanently delete a form together with its template.

A form that has already captured submissions cannot be deleted, so that the contacts it collected
are never silently discarded - pause the form instead to stop it collecting new ones. Views alone
do not block deletion.

actions.name: reach_update_form
actions.description:
Update form. Rename a form and/or change its status.

Setting a `draft` or `paused` form to `active` takes it live: its latest saved design is published
and visitors can submit it. `paused` and `draft` stop the form from accepting submissions. A form is
not reachable by visitors until it is taken live. Design changes saved while the form is already
`active` stay unpublished until the form is paused and set to `active` again. Renaming does not rename
the automatic `form:{name}` tag.

name.description: Form name. Letters, digits, spaces and - . ' _ only.

status.description: `active` takes the form live, `paused` and `draft` stop it accepting submissions.

actions.name: reach_duplicate_form
actions.description:
Duplicate form. Copy a form into a new draft form with the same name and design.

The copy shares the source's automatic `form:{name}` tag; other submitter tags are not copied. The
copy is not live until its status is set to `active`.

actions.name: reach_list_forms
actions.description:
List forms. Get a paginated list of the signup forms in a profile.

Each form carries a reference to the template that renders it. Get the form details for a
directly usable template URL and for the tags the form puts on the contacts it captures.

status.description: Return only forms with this status.

actions.name: reach_create_form
actions.description:
Create form. Create an empty draft form.

Reach also adds an automatic `form:{name}` tag that every submitter receives. A draft has no design
and is not reachable by visitors: save a design with the update form template operation, then take
the form live by setting its status to `active`. Creating a form does not consume AI credits.

name.description: Form name. Letters, digits, spaces and - . ' _ only.

actions.name: reach_add_form_submitter_tags
actions.description:
Add form submitter tags. Add tags to a form so that every contact who submits it from now on receives them.

A tag the form already has is skipped; an unknown tag is rejected. Contacts who submitted earlier are
not tagged.

actions.name: reach_remove_form_submitter_tag
actions.description:
Remove form submitter tag. Stop a form from applying a tag to its future submitters.

Succeeds also when the form did not have the tag. Contacts who already received the tag keep it, and
the tag itself is not deleted. The automatic `form:{name}` tag cannot be removed and is rejected with
a conflict.

actions.name: reach_update_form_template
actions.description:
Update form template. Save `content` as the latest design of a form and return the stored version.

The HTML is sanitized and, unless the plan allows removing it, the Reach signature is added. Visitors
submit the form with an `email` field (required) and optional `name`, `surname` and `phone`. After
sanitizing, the design must contain a form container (`data-reach-form`), an email input
(`data-reach-field="email"`) and a submit button (`data-reach-submit`); otherwise the request fails
with `422` and `errors.content` lists `missing_form_container`, `missing_email_field` and/or
`missing_submit_button`.

A `draft` or `paused` form stays unreachable until its status is set to `active`, which ...

content.description:
HTML of the form design. After sanitizing it must still contain a form container
(`data-reach-form`), an email input (`data-reach-field="email"`) and a submit button
(`data-reach-submit`).

actions.name: reach_get_connected_sending_domain
actions.description:
Get connected sending domain. Get the sending domain connected to the profile, its verification status and any suspended
sender addresses.

Campaigns only go out once a domain is connected and active, so this is the cheapest way to
check that precondition before building one. A profile with no domain connected returns the
same shape with every field set to `null`. For the individual MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records
behind the status, use the DNS status endpoint.

actions.name: reach_connect_sending_domain
actions.description:
Connect sending domain. Connect a sending domain to the profile so emails can be sent from addresses on it.

Connecting does not make the domain ready to send: check the DNS status endpoint next for
records that are still missing. A domain the account owns or has already verified connects
immediately. Any other domain starts a TXT ownership verification and returns `409`;
complete the verification in Reach, then retry. Returns `422` when the profile or another
profile already has the domain, the domain is blocked, or its ownership cannot be verified.
An already connected domain is never replaced.

On success the sender address of draft and scheduled campaigns, and of published automation
...

actions.name: reach_delete_sending_domain
actions.description:
Delete sending domain. Disconnect the sending domain from the profile.

The domain record is removed, so the profile has no sending domain afterwards and campaigns
cannot be sent until a domain is connected again. Sender addresses already stored on
campaigns, automations and settings are left untouched and keep pointing at the removed
domain. A domain that is not connected to the profile also succeeds, so success is not proof
that anything was deleted. DNS records at the DNS provider are not removed. To switch
domains, delete this one and connect the new one. Confirm the domain with the customer
before calling.

actions.name: reach_get_profile_domain_dns_status
actions.description:
Get profile domain DNS status. Retrieve the DNS configuration status for a profile's domain.

This endpoint reports the state of MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, including the
actual records found and the suggested records required for correct email delivery.

actions.name: reach_list_plan_feature_access
actions.description:
List plan feature access. List which plan features the profile can use.

This is the feature lock matrix, not a usage quota. `available` means the feature can be
used right now and `locked` means it is not part of the base plan, so an upgrade is needed.
For remaining emails, recipients and AI credits use the limits endpoint instead.

Worth checking before building something that cannot be activated afterwards, such as an
automation on a plan without automation activation.

actions.name: reach_get_remaining_plan_limits
actions.description:
Get remaining plan limits. Get how much of the plan is left for the current period.

Two things to keep in mind before you build alerting on this. The period is a calendar month
rather than a billing anniversary, so the counters reset on the 1st no matter when the
subscription started. And usage is tracked per order, so every profile on the same order shares
one pool and reports the same numbers here. Only the current period is available, past usage is
not kept.

actions.name: reach_list_profiles
actions.description: List Profiles. This endpoint returns all profiles available to the client, including their basic information.

actions.name: reach_get_profile_settings
actions.description:
Get profile settings. Get the profile's saved sender identity and brand details.

Read the default sender before creating a campaign instead of asking the customer, and
reuse the brand fields when generating email content. Any field can be `null` for a profile
that never filled its settings in. This does not check that the sending domain is
verified, use the connected sending domain endpoint for that.

actions.name: reach_update_profile_settings
actions.description:
Update profile settings. Change the profile's default sender and brand details.

Send only the fields to change: every omitted field keeps its value, and `null` or an empty
string clears a text field. The default sender is what campaigns created afterwards start
from; existing campaigns keep their own sender. `sender_email` is only the part before the
`@`, because Reach combines it with the profile's connected sending domain, so an address
outside that domain cannot be set. Connecting a sending domain is a separate endpoint and
a connected domain cannot be changed here. Returns the settings after the change.

logo_url.description: Public image URL. Logo uploads are not supported.

socials.description: Social profile links keyed by platform.

sender_name.description: Default sender name. Letters, numbers and spaces only.

sender_email.description:
Part of the default sender address before the `@`, for example `hello`. Never send a
full address: Reach adds the profile's connected sending domain itself.

actions.name: reach_list_email_templates
actions.description:
List email templates. Get a list of the email templates in a profile, most recently updated first.

Templates are the reusable email bodies a campaign is built from. The list is not paginated
and only the metadata is returned - the template content itself is not exposed. Use the
`uuid` of a template as the `template_uuid` when creating a campaign.

actions.name: reach_create_email_template
actions.description:
Create an email template in a profile.

The template holds the HTML body a campaign reuses, so it can be created before any
campaign exists. Only the template metadata comes back - keep the returned `uuid` to
reference it as the `template_uuid` of a campaign.

template_content.description:
The email body as HTML. It is sanitised before it is stored, so the saved template
can differ from what was sent - inline any styles the email clients need and keep
the markup self-contained.

title.description: Name the template is listed under. Not shown to the recipients.

actions.name: vps_get_data_center_list
actions.description:
Get data center list. Retrieve all available data centers.

Use this endpoint to view location options before deploying VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_get_project_containers
actions.description:
Get project containers. Retrieves a list of all containers belonging to a specific Docker Compose project on the virtual machine. 

This endpoint returns detailed information about each container including
their current status, port mappings, and runtime configuration.

Use this to monitor the health and state of all services within your Docker Compose project.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_get_project_contents
actions.description:
Get project contents. Retrieves the complete project information including the docker-compose.yml
file contents, project metadata, and current deployment status.

This endpoint provides the full configuration and state details of a specific Docker Compose project. 

Use this to inspect project settings, review the compose file, or check the overall project health.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_delete_project
actions.description:
Delete project. Completely removes a Docker Compose project from the virtual machine, stopping all containers and cleaning up 
associated resources including networks, volumes, and images. 

This operation is irreversible and will delete all project data. 

Use this when you want to permanently remove a project and free up system resources.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_get_project_list
actions.description:
Get project list. Retrieves a list of all Docker Compose projects currently deployed on the virtual machine. 

This endpoint returns basic information about each project including name,
status, file path and list of containers with details about their names,
image, status, health and ports. Container stats are omitted in this
endpoint. If you need to get detailed information about container with
stats included, use the `Get project containers` endpoint.

Use this to get an overview of all Docker projects on your VPS instance.

actions.name: vps_create_new_project
actions.description:
Create new project. Deploy new project from docker-compose.yaml contents or download contents from URL. 

URL can be Github repository url in format https://github.com/[user]/[repo]
and it will be automatically resolved to docker-compose.yaml file in
master branch. Any other URL provided must return docker-compose.yaml
file contents.

If project with the same name already exists, existing project will be replaced.

project_name.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

content.description: URL pointing to docker-compose.yaml file, Github repository or raw YAML content of the compose file

actions.name: vps_get_project_logs
actions.description:
Get project logs. Retrieves aggregated log entries from all services within a Docker Compose project. 

This endpoint returns recent log output from each container, organized by service name with timestamps. 
The response contains the last 300 log entries across all services. 

Use this for debugging, monitoring application behavior, and
troubleshooting issues across your entire project stack.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_restart_project
actions.description:
Restart project. Restarts all services in a Docker Compose project by stopping and starting
containers in the correct dependency order.

This operation preserves data volumes and network configurations while refreshing the running containers. 

Use this to apply configuration changes or recover from service failures.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_start_project
actions.description:
Start project. Starts all services in a Docker Compose project that are currently stopped. 

This operation brings up containers in the correct dependency order as defined in the compose file. 

Use this to resume a project that was previously stopped or to start services after a system reboot.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_stop_project
actions.description:
Stop project. Stops all running services in a Docker Compose project while preserving
container configurations and data volumes.

This operation gracefully shuts down containers in reverse dependency order. 

Use this to temporarily halt a project without removing data or configurations.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_update_project
actions.description:
Update project. Updates a Docker Compose project by pulling the latest image versions and
recreating containers with new configurations.

This operation preserves data volumes while applying changes from the compose file. 

Use this to deploy application updates, apply configuration changes, or
refresh container images to their latest versions.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

actions.name: vps_activate_firewall
actions.description:
Activate firewall. Activate a firewall for a specified virtual machine.

Only one firewall can be active for a virtual machine at a time.

Use this endpoint to apply firewall rules to VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_deactivate_firewall
actions.description:
Deactivate firewall. Deactivate a firewall for a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to remove firewall protection from VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_get_firewall_details
actions.description:
Get firewall details. Retrieve firewall by its ID and rules associated with it.

Use this endpoint to view specific firewall configuration and rules.

actions.name: vps_delete_firewall
actions.description:
Delete firewall. Delete a specified firewall.

Any virtual machine that has this firewall activated will automatically have it deactivated.

Use this endpoint to remove unused firewall configurations.

actions.name: vps_get_firewall_list
actions.description:
Get firewall list. Retrieve all available firewalls.

Use this endpoint to view existing firewall configurations.

actions.name: vps_create_new_firewall
actions.description:
Create new firewall. Create a new firewall.

Use this endpoint to set up new firewall configurations for VPS security.

actions.name: vps_update_firewall_rule
actions.description:
Update firewall rule. Update a specific firewall rule from a specified firewall.

Any virtual machine that has this firewall activated will lose sync with the firewall
and will have to be synced again manually.

Use this endpoint to modify existing firewall rules.

source_detail.description: IP range, CIDR, single IP or `any`

actions.name: vps_delete_firewall_rule
actions.description:
Delete firewall rule. Delete a specific firewall rule from a specified firewall.

Any virtual machine that has this firewall activated will lose sync with the firewall
and will have to be synced again manually.

Use this endpoint to remove specific firewall rules.

actions.name: vps_replace_all_firewall_rules_in_group
actions.description:
Replace all firewall rules in group. Replaces all firewall rules within a specified firewall group with the provided set of rules
in a single atomic operation, instead of creating or deleting rules one by one.

Any virtual machine using this firewall group will need to be synchronized after replacing rules;
pass the "sync" parameter to trigger synchronization immediately.

rules.description: The complete set of firewall rules that atomically replaces all existing rules in the group

source_detail.description: IP range, CIDR, single IP or `any`

sync.description: Synchronize the firewall group to all its virtual machines after replacing the rules

actions.name: vps_create_firewall_rule
actions.description:
Create firewall rule. Create new firewall rule for a specified firewall.

By default, the firewall drops all incoming traffic,
which means you must add accept rules for all ports you want to use.

Any virtual machine that has this firewall activated will lose sync with the firewall
and will have to be synced again manually.

Use this endpoint to add new security rules to firewalls.

source_detail.description: IP range, CIDR, single IP or `any`

actions.name: vps_sync_firewall_to_all_assigned_vms
actions.description:
Sync firewall to all assigned VMs. Sync a firewall's rules to every virtual machine it's assigned to.

Firewall can lose sync with a virtual machine if the firewall has new rules added, removed or updated.

Use this endpoint to apply updated firewall rules to all VPS instances assigned to the firewall.

actions.name: vps_get_post_install_script
actions.description:
Get post-install script. Retrieve post-install script by its ID.

Use this endpoint to view specific automation script details.

actions.name: vps_update_post_install_script
actions.description:
Update post-install script. Update a specific post-install script.

Use this endpoint to modify existing automation scripts.

name.description: Name of the script

actions.name: vps_delete_post_install_script
actions.description:
Delete post-install script. Delete a post-install script from your account.
       
Use this endpoint to remove unused automation scripts.

actions.name: vps_get_post_install_scripts
actions.description:
Get post-install scripts. Retrieve post-install scripts associated with your account.

Use this endpoint to view available automation scripts for VPS deployment.

actions.name: vps_create_post_install_script
actions.description:
Create post-install script. Add a new post-install script to your account, which can then be used after virtual machine installation.

The script contents will be saved to the file `/post_install` with executable attribute set
and will be executed once virtual machine is installed.
The output of the script will be redirected to `/post_install.log`. Maximum script size is 48KB.

Use this endpoint to create automation scripts for VPS setup tasks.

name.description: Name of the script

actions.name: vps_list_virtual_machine_ssh_keys
actions.description:
List virtual machine SSH keys. Retrieve SSH public keys currently configured on a specified virtual machine.

Only keys of the `root` user are listed.

Use this endpoint to view SSH keys that can be used for authentication on VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_add_virtual_machine_ssh_keys
actions.description:
Add virtual machine SSH keys. Add one or more SSH public keys to a specified virtual machine.

Keys are added to the `root` user and can be used for passwordless SSH authentication.
Returns the complete list of SSH keys currently configured on the virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to enable SSH key authentication for VPS instances.

keys.description: SSH public keys in OpenSSH format to add

actions.name: vps_remove_virtual_machine_ssh_keys
actions.description:
Remove virtual machine SSH keys. Remove one or more SSH public keys from a specified virtual machine.

Removed keys can no longer be used to authenticate via SSH as the `root` user.
Returns the remaining list of SSH keys configured on the virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to revoke SSH key access to VPS instances.

keys.description: SSH public keys in OpenSSH format to remove

actions.name: vps_get_template_details
actions.description:
Get template details. Retrieve detailed information about a specific OS template for virtual machines.

Use this endpoint to view specific template specifications before deployment.

actions.name: vps_get_templates
actions.description:
Get templates. Retrieve available OS templates for virtual machines.

Use this endpoint to view operating system options before creating or recreating VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_get_action_details
actions.description:
Get action details. Retrieve detailed information about a specific action performed on a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to monitor specific VPS operation status and details.

actions.name: vps_get_actions
actions.description:
Get actions. Retrieve actions performed on a specified virtual machine.

Actions are operations or events that have been executed on the virtual
machine, such as starting, stopping, or modifying the machine. This endpoint
allows you to view the history of these actions, providing details about
each action, such as the action name, timestamp, and status.

Use this endpoint to view VPS operation history and troubleshoot issues.

actions.name: vps_get_backups
actions.description:
Get backups. Retrieve backups for a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to view available backup points for VPS data recovery.

actions.name: vps_restore_backup
actions.description:
Restore backup. Restore a backup for a specified virtual machine.

The system will then initiate the restore process, which may take some time depending on the size of the backup.

**All data on the virtual machine will be overwritten with the data from the backup.**

Use this endpoint to recover VPS data from backup points.

actions.name: vps_set_hostname
actions.description:
Set hostname for a specified virtual machine.

Changing hostname does not update PTR record automatically.
If you want your virtual machine to be reachable by a hostname, 
you need to point your domain A/AAAA records to virtual machine IP as well.

Use this endpoint to configure custom hostnames for VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_reset_hostname
actions.description:
Reset hostname and PTR record of a specified virtual machine to default value.

Use this endpoint to restore default hostname configuration for VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_get_virtual_machine_details
actions.description:
Get virtual machine details. Retrieve detailed information about a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to view comprehensive VPS configuration and status.

actions.name: vps_get_virtual_machines
actions.description:
Get virtual machines. Retrieve all available virtual machines.

Use this endpoint to view available VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_purchase_new_virtual_machine
actions.description:
Purchase new virtual machine. Purchase and setup a new virtual machine.

If virtual machine setup fails for any reason, login to
[hPanel](https://hpanel.hostinger.com/) and complete the setup manually.

If no payment method is provided, your default payment method will be used automatically.

If the response is `202 Accepted`, the payment is still being processed and the virtual machine
was not set up. Login to
[hPanel](https://hpanel.hostinger.com/) and complete the setup manually.

Use this endpoint to create new VPS instances.

payment_method_id.description: Payment method ID, default will be used if not provided

password.description:
Password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated.
Password will not be shown in the response.

hostname.description: Override default hostname of the virtual machine

name.description: Name of the SSH key

actions.name: vps_get_scan_metrics
actions.description:
Get scan metrics. Retrieve scan metrics for the [Monarx](https://www.monarx.com/) malware scanner
installed on a specified virtual machine.

The scan metrics provide detailed information about malware scans performed
by Monarx, including number of scans, detected threats, and other relevant
statistics. This information is useful for monitoring security status of the
virtual machine and assessing effectiveness of the malware scanner.

Use this endpoint to monitor VPS security scan results and threat detection.

actions.name: vps_install_monarx
actions.description:
Install Monarx. Install the Monarx malware scanner on a specified virtual machine.

[Monarx](https://www.monarx.com/) is a security tool designed to detect and
prevent malware infections on virtual machines. By installing Monarx, users
can enhance the security of their virtual machines, ensuring that they are
protected against malicious software.

Use this endpoint to enable malware protection on VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_uninstall_monarx
actions.description:
Uninstall Monarx. Uninstall the Monarx malware scanner on a specified virtual machine.

If Monarx is not installed, the request will still be processed without any effect.

Use this endpoint to remove malware scanner from VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_get_metrics
actions.description:
Get metrics. Retrieve historical metrics for a specified virtual machine.

It includes the following metrics: 
- CPU usage
- Memory usage
- Disk usage
- Network usage
- Uptime

Use this endpoint to monitor VPS performance and resource utilization over time.

actions.name: vps_set_nameservers
actions.description:
Set nameservers for a specified virtual machine.

Be aware, that improper nameserver configuration can lead to the virtual
machine being unable to resolve domain names.

Use this endpoint to configure custom DNS resolvers for VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_create_ptr_record
actions.description:
Create PTR record. Create or update a PTR (Pointer) record for a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to configure reverse DNS lookup for VPS IP addresses.

actions.name: vps_delete_ptr_record
actions.description:
Delete PTR record. Delete a PTR (Pointer) record for a specified virtual machine.

Once deleted, reverse DNS lookups to the virtual machine's IP address will
no longer return the previously configured hostname.

Use this endpoint to remove reverse DNS configuration from VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_set_panel_password
actions.description:
Set panel password for a specified virtual machine.

If virtual machine does not use panel OS, the request will still be processed without any effect.
Requirements for password are same as in the [recreate virtual machine
endpoint](/#tag/vps-virtual-machine/POST/api/vps/v1/virtual-machines/{virtualMachineId}/recreate).

Use this endpoint to configure control panel access credentials for VPS instances.

password.description: Panel password for the virtual machine

actions.name: vps_start_recovery_mode
actions.description:
Start recovery mode. Initiate recovery mode for a specified virtual machine.

Recovery mode is a special state that allows users to perform system rescue operations, 
such as repairing file systems, recovering data, or troubleshooting issues that prevent the virtual machine 
from booting normally. 

Virtual machine will boot recovery disk image and original disk image will be mounted in `/mnt` directory.

Use this endpoint to enable system rescue operations on VPS instances.

root_password.description: Temporary root password for recovery mode

actions.name: vps_stop_recovery_mode
actions.description:
Stop recovery mode for a specified virtual machine.

If virtual machine is not in recovery mode, this operation will fail.

Use this endpoint to exit system rescue mode and return VPS to normal operation.

actions.name: vps_recreate_virtual_machine
actions.description:
Recreate virtual machine. Recreate a virtual machine from scratch.

The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and
resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 12 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

Use this endpoint to completely rebuild VPS instances with fresh OS installation.

password.description:
Root password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated.
Password will not be shown in the response.

panel_password.description:
Panel password for the panel-based OS template. If not provided, random password will be generated.
If OS does not support panel_password this field will be ignored.
Password will not be shown in the response.

post_install_script_id.description: Post-install script to execute after virtual machine was recreated

actions.name: vps_restart_virtual_machine
actions.description:
Restart virtual machine. Restart a specified virtual machine by fully stopping and starting it.

If the virtual machine was stopped, it will be started.

Use this endpoint to reboot VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_set_root_password
actions.description:
Set root password for a specified virtual machine.

Requirements for password are same as in the [recreate virtual machine
endpoint](/#tag/vps-virtual-machine/POST/api/vps/v1/virtual-machines/{virtualMachineId}/recreate).

Use this endpoint to update administrator credentials for VPS instances.

password.description: Root password for the virtual machine

actions.name: vps_setup_purchased_virtual_machine
actions.description:
Setup purchased virtual machine. Setup newly purchased virtual machine with `initial` state.

Use this endpoint to configure and initialize purchased VPS instances.

password.description:
Password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated.
Password will not be shown in the response.

hostname.description: Override default hostname of the virtual machine

name.description: Name of the SSH key

actions.name: vps_get_snapshot
actions.description:
Get snapshot. Retrieve snapshot for a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to view current VPS snapshot information.

actions.name: vps_create_snapshot
actions.description:
Create snapshot. Create a snapshot of a specified virtual machine.

A snapshot captures the state and data of the virtual machine at a specific point in time, 
allowing users to restore the virtual machine to that state if needed. 
This operation is useful for backup purposes, system recovery, 
and testing changes without affecting the current state of the virtual machine.

**Creating new snapshot will overwrite the existing snapshot!**

Use this endpoint to capture VPS state for backup and recovery purposes.

actions.name: vps_delete_snapshot
actions.description:
Delete snapshot. Delete a snapshot of a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to remove VPS snapshots.

actions.name: vps_restore_snapshot
actions.description:
Restore snapshot. Restore a specified virtual machine to a previous state using a snapshot.

Restoring from a snapshot allows users to revert the virtual machine to that state,
which is useful for system recovery, undoing changes, or testing.

Use this endpoint to revert VPS instances to previous saved states.

actions.name: vps_start_virtual_machine
actions.description:
Start virtual machine. Start a specified virtual machine.

If the virtual machine is already running, the request will still be processed without any effect.

Use this endpoint to power on stopped VPS instances.

actions.name: vps_stop_virtual_machine
actions.description:
Stop virtual machine. Stop a specified virtual machine.

If the virtual machine is already stopped, the request will still be processed without any effect.

This is a compute-only power state change and does not affect billing. To stop future charges,
disable auto-renewal on the owning subscription.

Use this endpoint to power off running VPS instances.

actions.name: hosting_generate_images
actions.description:
Generate images. Start generating one or more images from a prompt and an image type for the specified
WordPress installation. The generation runs asynchronously: the response is returned
right away with `status: in-progress` and a `generation_id`. Poll
GET /api/hosting/v1/accounts/{username}/wordpress/{software}/content/generations/{generation_id}
every few seconds until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.

A completed generation returns temporary image URLs together with the time they expire;
download the images before then. Images match the requested aspect ratio and are never
smaller than the requested size; logos are transparent images cropped to the mark.

Only one image generation...

prompt.description: What the image should show. For the logo type, the wordmark and mark to render.

image_type.description: Kind of image to generate. It sets the default size and cropping.

width.description: Output width in pixels. Defaults per image type and is ignored for the logo type.

height.description: Output height in pixels. Defaults per image type and is ignored for the logo type.

style.description: Style tokens appended to photographic prompts. Ignored for the logo type.

color_guidance.description: Colour direction for the logo type only. It is not rendered as text.

actions.name: hosting_get_generation_result
actions.description:
Get generation result. Get the result of an AI content generation started for the specified WordPress
installation, such as an image generation started with
POST /api/hosting/v1/accounts/{username}/wordpress/{software}/content/images/generate.

While the generation is still running only `status: in-progress` is returned; poll every
few seconds. Once `completed`, `result` holds the generated content shaped according to
`type`: temporary image URLs together with the time they expire for `image-generation`, or
the generated website document for `website-generation` (started from the Hostinger
WordPress plugin). A `failed` generation has no `result`. Unknown or expired generation
IDs return 4...

generation_id.description: Generation ID returned when the generation was started

type.description: Generation type to look up. When omitted, every generation type is checked.

actions.name: hosting_show_ai_option_status
actions.description:
Show AI option status. Show the current AI option status for the Hostinger Tools plugin on the
specified WordPress installation. Filter by `option` to return a single
option, or omit it to return all options.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field).

option.description: Filter the status by a single AI option.

actions.name: hosting_set_ai_option_status
actions.description:
Set AI option status. Enable or disable an AI option for the Hostinger Tools plugin on the specified
WordPress installation.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field).

enable.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) the AI option.

actions.name: hosting_check_if_wordpress_installations_are_valid
actions.description:
Check if WordPress installations are valid. Check whether one or more WordPress installations are valid and working
correctly. Detects broken installations caused by missing files, broken
plugins, themes and similar issues.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifiers in the body. They
can be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id`
field).

force.description: Force fresh validation without cache. Preferable for troubleshooting purposes.

actions.name: hosting_delete_wordpress_installation
actions.description:
Delete WordPress installation. Delete the specified WordPress installation, with optional file and database
removal. This removes all associated components including plugins, themes,
staging websites and any other related data.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field).

actions.name: hosting_detect_wordpress_installations
actions.description:
Detect WordPress installations. Trigger a background scan to detect WordPress installations for the account.

This operation is asynchronous: a successful response only means the scan has
been queued. Poll GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations to fetch the
detected installations once the scan completes.

actions.name: hosting_import_wordpress_website
actions.description:
Import WordPress website to the specified domain.

WARNING: this overwrites the website's existing contents and cannot be undone —
verify this is intended before calling this endpoint.

This endpoint allows you to import a WordPress website from archive and
database files that have been uploaded to the website's directory.

archive_path.description: Path to the WordPress archive file (relative to website root)

sql_path.description: Path to the database SQL file (relative to website root)

actions.name: hosting_install_wordpress
actions.description:
Install WordPress on an existing website.

The website must already exist before calling this endpoint. To create a new
website first, use POST /api/hosting/v1/orders/{order_id}/onboardings
(`hosting_websites_start-setup`) and poll GET /api/hosting/v1/onboardings
(`hosting_websites_list-setups`) with the `domain` filter until its `status` is
`completed`.

Send `type: headless` to turn a headless website (for example one created by
`hosting_websites_start-setup` with `type: headless_empty`) into a headless WordPress
website: WordPress is installed into the `cms` directory with the Hostinger headless
MU plugin and the website is marked as a headless WordPress website. `directory` is
not all...

domain.description: Domain of the existing website where WordPress will be installed

language.description: WordPress locale. Defaults to en_US when omitted.

type.description: Installation kind; `default` when omitted. `headless` installs WordPress into the `cms` directory with the Hostinger headless MU plugin and marks the website as a headless WordPress website. Accepted only for a website that is already headless, e.g. one created by `POST /api/hosting/v1/orders/{order_id}/onboardings` (`hosting_websites_start-setup`) with `type: headless_empty`; any other website is rejected with 422.

directory.description: Installation subdirectory relative to the document root; omit for the root. Not allowed with `type: headless`, which always installs into `cms`.

overwrite.description: When false (default), does not replace an existing installation. If WordPress is already installed on the domain/path, the async install job fails unless true.

version.description: WordPress core version to install. If omitted, the latest core version compatible with the account vhost PHP version is selected.

database.description: Optional. If the named database already exists on the account, it is used for this WordPress install. Otherwise a new database is created with this name, or with a generated name when database is omitted or null. A new database gets a random database user and counts toward the plan's database limit.

name.description: Database name (username prefix added if missing)

password.description: Password for a new database. Random when omitted or null. Ignored when the named database already exists.

actions.name: hosting_list_wordpress_installations
actions.description:
List WordPress installations on shared and cloud web hosting accounts (the
`/api/hosting/v1` family, identified by `username`) accessible to the
authenticated client.

Agency Plan websites are not included. To work with WordPress on an Agency Plan
website, list them with GET /api/agency-hosting/v1/websites?website_types=wordpress
and read their details with
GET /api/agency-hosting/v1/websites/{website_uid}/wordpress/settings. An account
that only has Agency Plan websites receives an empty list from this endpoint.

Use this endpoint to discover existing WordPress installations and to poll
for installation status after calling the install endpoint. When a newly
requested installation appear...

domain.description: Filter by domain name (case-insensitive substring match)

ownership.description: Filter by ownership type. Defaults to "owned". Use "all" to include both owned and managed installations.

actions.name: hosting_list_available_wordpress_core_updates
actions.description:
List available WordPress core updates for the specified installation.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field).

actions.name: hosting_get_installation_jwt_token
actions.description:
Get installation JWT token. Return a JWT token used to authenticate requests against the specified
WordPress installation, including its MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field). Shows a secret: only when the person needs it, never pasted in a chat.

actions.name: hosting_show_wordpress_core_version
actions.description:
Show WordPress core version. Show the WordPress core version for the specified installation, along with
known vulnerabilities affecting it.

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field).

actions.name: hosting_update_wordpress_core
actions.description:
Update WordPress core. Update the WordPress core for the specified installation (minor update or a
specific version).

Provide the WordPress installation (software) identifier in the path. It can
be obtained from GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations (the `id` field).

This operation is asynchronous: a successful response only means the update
job has been queued.

version.description: Update to a specific WordPress core version.

actions.name: hosting_purge_litespeed_cache
actions.description:
Purge LiteSpeed Cache. Purge the LiteSpeed Cache for the specified WordPress installation.
